title: Check PCSX2 configuration before booting a game
summary: Run the documented `-testconfig` startup check to initialize and check the PCSX2 configuration version without opening a game.
heroAlt: Top side of a PlayStation 2 Slim motherboard.
author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: check pcsx2 configuration before a game launch
Check PCSX2 configuration before booting a game

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents `-testconfig` as initializing its configuration and checking its version before exiting. It is a narrow startup diagnostic: it does not test a BIOS boot, game image, graphics renderer, controller, or save. Use it when a launch environment needs a quick configuration check, then test the actual component that is failing separately.

Close all PCSX2 instances and back up configuration data you care about. Use the same executable and data-folder switches as your normal launch; otherwise you may check a different installation or profile. Do not add a game filename, because this check is intended to initialize and exit rather than boot a title.

items: 1. Record the executable path and any `-portable` or `-datapath` option used by your normal shortcut.
2. Copy the shortcut or command so the regular launcher is preserved.
3. Add `-testconfig` and keep the same data-folder options in the copied command.
4. Run the command once and wait for it to exit.
5. Note any error text and inspect the same data folder for recent configuration activity.
6. Remove the test switch and start PCSX2 normally; then boot a lawful game image only if the ordinary launch succeeds.

blocks.text: The check passes when PCSX2 exits without a configuration error and the normal application opens afterward using the same data path. This confirms configuration initialization/version checking only. A successful result does not prove that BIOS, games, controllers, or renderers work.

items: No visible result: check the executable path and run the copied command from a terminal to observe exit output.
A different profile appears: compare portable/datapath arguments with the normal shortcut.
The normal launch now behaves differently: restore the backed-up configuration before trying further changes.
The game still fails: keep this result as one diagnostic and investigate the game boot path separately.

blocks.text: Remove `-testconfig` from the copied command and return to the unchanged normal shortcut. If an unexpected configuration change occurred, restore your backup while PCSX2 is closed. Do not delete the active data directory as a reset shortcut.
